An Elstree Childhood
Saturday 10th October 2026
Welcome
Elstree is a Preparatory School for children aged 2 – 13 years.
It is our privilege and responsibility to equip pupils with the skills, knowledge and character that they will need to serve their community and thrive in our ever-changing world.
Set within 150 acres of idyllic Berkshire countryside, we proudly combine academic rigour with outstanding co-curricular opportunities – and we never forget the magic of a proper childhood.
An ethos of hard work, a purposeful culture and crucially, an all-encompassing atmosphere of kindness and encouragement set Elstree apart.
Sid Inglis HEADMASTER
1. An extended family
Fundamental to Elstree is our sense of community and camaraderie amongst pupils, staff, parents and alumni.
We take every opportunity to get to know each of the 300 children in our care. Loyalty and a sense of belonging are strengthened through our House system, ensuring close and lasting bonds are formed.
We welcome parents as active participants in school life and delight in the many friendships that are formed between families.
We are proud that so many Old Boys and Girls choose Elstree for their children, sharing the same memories of childhood, learning and Christian values that have long been at the heart of the Elstree ethos.
2. Academic rigour in a supportive environment
At Elstree we craft a bespoke academic journey for each child.
Average class sizes of just 14 enable us to provide expert teaching and attention; stretching each individual pupil in a way that works for them.
Our pupils are encouraged and challenged to work hard within a culture of ambition. This is rewarded with an outstanding record of Scholarship success to leading Senior Schools.
We take pastoral care seriously. Our Deputy Head - Pastoral and our Head of Pupil Wellbeing and Mental Health are both members of the Senior Management Team. They are joined by two Emotional Literacy Support Assistants.
The support we offer ensures every child will flourish to the best of their ability.
3. Unforgettable games in glorious grounds
There is a magic to a childhood spent in Elstree’s 150 acres of beautiful grounds.
Along with ample space for sports pitches and matches galore, our grounds include two lakes for paddle-boarding, canoeing and raft-building. The children enjoy parkland for outdoor education, bushcraft, mountain biking and great games of Capture-the-Flag. Our woodland plays host to Early Years learning, den building and marshmallows around a campfire.
These experiences form enduring happy memories, but also play a crucial role in developing key skills such as teamwork, resilience and creativity.
And yes, after the games, there are endless opportunities for Music, Drama, Art and DT in the practice rooms, studios and performance halls too!
4. The best of boarding
Elstree is a second home for boarders and non-boarders alike.
Being a boarding school goes beyond simply offering pupils overnight accommodation: we strive to maximise the experiences and opportunities that a boarding ethos allows.
We believe in flexibility and seek the best set up for each child and their family, at each step of their journey with us. By ensuring consistency and familiarity, close friendships and happy memories are made.
More than half of Elstree children board in some capacity - up to 90 children on any given night - so it’s clear that the children and their families welcome the fun and independence that is fostered through this special opportunity.
5. Firm foundations for the future
The responsibility of advising on the best Senior School for each child is something we take incredibly seriously.
Proudly leading Elstree for over 10 years, Sid and Olivia Inglis have developed strong and longstanding partnerships with top Senior Schools in the country. Advice and guidance is based on personal knowledge of each pupil, combined with seeking the best possible match for their onward success.
We delight in the feedback we receive from Senior Schools on the outstanding contributions that Elstree alumni make to their schools. We are proud that Elstree leavers are kind and confident individuals with a range of passions and talents, united by positivity, compassion and humility.

Visit us
We believe the best way to get a taste of life at Elstree is to visit! Come along to one of our Open Mornings or book a private tour at a time to suit you. Both are ideal opportunities to meet the Headmaster, teaching and admissions staff and of course, get a first-hand view of the school. We would love to show you around!

Staff & Governors
Senior Leadership Team
Sid Inglis
Sid Inglis
Sid Inglis was educated at Radley College and Newcastle University, where he read Religious Studies. His teaching career started in Santiago, Chile where he spent two years teaching English at Redland School. He also gained three International cricket caps for Chile during this period.
In 1995, Sid moved to Ludgrove where he taught Classics before being promoted to Assistant Headmaster and then Joint Headmaster in 2008.
In September 2013, Sid was appointed Headmaster of Elstree School. The School is thriving with 300 girls and boys enjoying an Elstree childhood. Recently awarded Best Prep School Headmaster of the Year by Tatler Schools Awards, Sid is recognised for being ambitious for each and every pupil, as well as offering encyclopaedic and personal advice on Senior Schools.
Sid and Olivia have three children. Sid is a member of the School Chapel Choir and enjoys coaching sports when time allows. A keen sportsman himself, particularly cricket and golf; Sid especially likes to go fishing near his family home in Wales.
Olivia Inglis
Olivia Inglis
Olivia Inglis grew up in Yorkshire and was educated at Wycombe Abbey and Durham University, where she graduated with a First-Class degree in Modern Languages (French and Spanish).
An early career in Marketing led to a position as Premium Brands Director at a small Luxury Brand Development Agency overseeing the strategy for brands including Red Bull, Veuve Clicquot and Boodles.
Working closely with Sid, Olivia oversees so much of School life at Elstree. She unites parents and staff to form committees that are integral to Elstree’s welcoming and fun community and do so much to support local charities. Olivia manages the School Dining Room committee, making sure nutritious and tasty meals are a staple for good health and happy children. Olivia also teaches French to Year 8, prepares children for Church readings on Saturdays and oversees Senior School interview practice for all Year 6 pupils.
Olivia lives at Elstree, with her husband Sid. Her happiest moments are being together with their three children Eliza, Johnny and Tom. She has a keen interest in photography and loves to cook and entertain. Travel, keeping fit, reading and languages are all active hobbies.
Simon Attwood
Simon Attwood
Simon was educated at Colston’s School and Clifton College in Bristol, before university in London at the Roehampton Institute. He began his teaching career at Elstree School in West Berkshire as Boarding Housemaster and Head of English, before moving to Windlesham House School in West Sussex as Deputy Headmaster.
He rejoined Elstree in 2016 and is currently the Senior Deputy Headmaster at the school. Simon is married with two grown-up children. His interests are his family, rugby, cricket, music, reading and camping, and he remains an enthusiastic sailor.
Simon joined The Downs Malvern as a Governor in October 2022 and is the school’s Boarding Governor.
Alice Bond
Alice Bond
Alice grew up in and around the local area. She went to school at Headington Girls’ School in Oxford before attending Nottingham Trent University where she embarked on a four year degree in teaching.
Alice took up her first post at Chandlings School in Abingdon before moving to Garden House School in Chelsea, London. Alice stayed in London for seven years, class teaching before becoming the Head of English and the Director of Teaching and Learning, overseeing the academics from Nursery to Year 6.
In 2019, Alice and her now-husband left London to live in the countryside. She first visited Elstree one rainy day in April, however, she fell in love with the warm and welcoming feel of the school and knew it was the place for her to further her career. She was delighted to be appointed Head of Pre-Prep.
Alice has a daughter, Cecily, a son, Bertie, and a very energetic cocker-spaniel. When not teaching, Alice can be found playing with her children, baking a cake or, in the holidays, enjoying the snow in the mountains.
Will Aird
Will Aird
William Aird rejoined Elstree in January 2023.
He is an Elstree Old Boy (1974-1980) who now lives in Wolverton Common with his wife Lilia and two daughters.
He left Elstree for Radley and then went on to Christ Church, Oxford to read Natural Sciences. William is a Chartered Accountant with over 30 years experience in consulting, brewing and cybersecurity. He spent most of his corporate career working throughout the CIS.
William spends his spare time travelling, playing bridge and loves films. He also part owns a small boutique hotel in Tallinn, Estonia.

James Sunley
James Sunley is an Elstree Old Boy (1971-1975) who lives near Hungerford in West Berkshire with his wife Lisa and four children. He became Chair of Governors for Elstree in 2014.
James runs a family property, development and venture capital business. A product of Oxford and Reading Universities, James is especially interested in environmental matters and the advances of technology which help improve educational methods, healthcare and standards of living.
An enthusiastic sportsman, especially cycling, golf and skiing, James held the top Cresta Run record for 16 years, and has been President of The St Moritz Tobogganing Club since 2014. He is also a proud part owner of a small Burgundian vineyard.

Gavin Owston
Gavin has educated all of his three children at Elstree.
Having spent 20 years in investment banking, he is now a partner of a UK based private investment firm in London. He makes investments in telecom, media, technology, education and business services companies.
He is inspired by the passion of the teachers at Elstree and in awe of the energy all the children exude at the school. Gavin joined the Elstree board of Governors in 2015 and chairs the Finance and General Purposes committee.
Pippa Foulds
Member of the Finance & General Purposes Committee, Member of the Marketing Committee
Pippa Foulds
Pippa Foulds was educated at Benenden School and Edinburgh University, where she read Economics and Economic History.
After University, Pippa qualified as a Chartered Accountant at Arthur Andersen before a career in Investor Relations at BAA, EMI and now at ITV where she has been Director of Investor Relations for almost 10 years.
Pippa is married to Mark, with two children Wilf and Aggie. Wilf left Elstree in 2024 and Aggie is currently at Elstree. Pippa is a keen sportswomen, particularly tennis, skiing and sailing and loves cooking for friends and family.
Chris Houston
Member of the Finance & General Purposes Committee, Member of the Health & Safety Committee
Chris Houston
Chris was educated at Leighton Park School in Reading and Corpus Christi College, Cambridge. He spent his career in investment banking and held senior positions at Schroders, Citigroup, Lexicon Partners and Evercore. His job was to advise governments, companies and financial investors on the financing, sale, acquisition and restructuring of major infrastructure assets around the world. He was based in London for much of his career but worked in South East Asia for many years and has lived in Hong Kong, Singapore and Kuala Lumpur.
Chris was a governor of Leighton Park School from 2016 to 2023. He was Vice Chair of the Board and Chair of the Business Committee for six years.
Chris is married to Jill, an artisan flower farmer. They have three children and live in Brimpton. Their two sons were at Elstree between 2008 and 2017.
Juliet Joynson
Member of the Academic Committee
Juliet Joynson
Juliet Joynson, BA Hons, Dip SpLD. With 20 years of experience supporting children’s learning, Juliet is the Head of Learning Support in the Upper Prep at Thomas’s Battersea, London.
Juliet and her husband, Michael have three sons and live in south west London. She is a keen skier, enthusiastic cook and passionate advocate for neurodiversity.
Juliet joined the Elstree Governors in 2020 and supports the Elstree Pre-Prep, sitting on the Academic committee.
Jane Lyons
Member of the Safeguarding & Pastoral Committee, Member of the Marketing Committee, Member of the Health & Safety Committee, Member of the Legal & Governance Committee
Jane Lyons
Married with three children, both of Jane’s boys experienced many happy years at Elstree.
Jane attended LAMDA and after a short acting career worked in PR. Jane has spent 35 years working as a volunteer raising money for charities, mainly for NSPCC and St Michael’s Hospice , Basingstoke where she is a Trustee. Jane is also Chairman of The Friends of SMH and was awarded an MBE in 2020.
Jane joined the Elstree as a Governor in 2015 and supports the Marketing and Pastoral commitees. It remains her pleasure to serve this wonderful school.
Emma McKendrick
Member of the Academic Committee
Emma McKendrick
Emma McKendrick was educated at Bedford High School and then went to Liverpool University. She began her teaching career at the Royal School in Bath where she progressed to her first Headship. In 1997 she took up her role as Head of Downe House where she remains.
She has served as a Governor at a number of Prep Schools and Senior Schools, including King’s College, Canterbury, Radley College and she is currently on the Board of Wellington College. She has also served on the GSA Education Committee, the Independent Schools’ Examination Board Council and is a Trustee of the Prep School Baccalaureate. She is married to Iain and has two sons, both of whom went to Elstree.
Emma is a Fellow of the Royal Society of Arts and loves going to the theatre, opera and travelling, as well as eating out with friends and family. She particularly enjoys visiting their home in Southwold in Suffolk.
Joining the Elstree board in 2018, Emma serves on the Academic committee.
James McKinnel
Member of the Academic Committee, Member of the Safeguarding & Pastoral Committee
James McKinnel
James was educated at King’s College Taunton and St Andrew’s University, where he read History. He captained the St Andrew’s 1st XV and played flyhalf for Scotland Students, and then Oxford University Blues.
He began his career as a solicitor in Hampshire after spending a year teaching English at Elstree in 2012. The ‘Elstree year’ was to prove hugely formative and he moved from the law to take up the post of Head of History at Ludgrove in 2014. In 2018 he was appointed a History Don and Lay Chaplain at Winchester College, and shortly afterwards Housemaster Elect of Turner’s beginning September 2023.
James was ordained by the Church of England in July, and regularly preaches at schools and churches in the region. Married to Holly, with two small boys, James is a very keen sportsman, particularly cricket and running, and enjoys trying to outwit the trout on the Itchen and near his family home in Devon. He also fulfils various charity roles including for the Church Pastoral Aid Society and the Crown and Manor Club.
He joined the governing body in late 2022 and supports the Academic committee.

With a strong foundation of academic excellence, personal guidance, and character development, they leave confident, capable, and ready to thrive in the next stage of their education. Our record of Leavers’ Destinations and Scholarship Results speak for themselves.

The boys from Elstree that we have welcomed to Winchester in recent years have, without exception, thrived here. They tend to make the step up to a more independent way of learning more easily than some and demonstrate a real desire to achieve. This often comes across in their work ethic, but also in the way they take to full boarding and adapt to organisational challenges of the bigger school set up.
It seems to me that the culture at Elstree is one of kindness, busyness and curiosity, and these are traits we often see in the boys that make their way to us. Often that means the individuals will throw themselves into their subjects, make friends quickly and make important contributions musically or on the sports fields whether it’s their ‘thing’ or not. They participate and are busy – and often a busy child is a happy child.
I regularly interview boys for the boarding house and always look forward to seeing an Elstree boy in my diary.
Elstree boys in Common Lane are extremely polite, well-rounded characters who act with upmost integrity. I have been hugely impressed with their willingness to engage in so many aspects of Eton life, such as the arts, sports and societies. They embrace new experiences and capitalise on opportunities which come their way.
Half of the Common Lane House leadership team is made up of boys from Elstree. They show great initiative in their roles and have proposed innovative ideas to take house events to that next level.
Elstree boys manage to combine a strong work ethic with a fine sense of humour and a healthy level of house spirit. Whilst they are ambitious, aspirational young men, I am always struck by their willingness to help those around them. Elstree boys seem to make friends easily owing to their fine interpersonal skills and respectful nature.
For many years I have been aware that the extraordinary sense of place and the balance of the academic, co-curricular and pastoral life at Elstree has produced really well-rounded and generous spirited young people.
When Elstree pupils arrive at Marlborough they know how to work hard, take up challenges, help others, make new friends and have fun. They are great to have around. It is clear the school has gone from strength to strength and the move to co-education has enriched the school in many ways: we are delighted to be welcoming a stream of Elstree girls too.
It has been my privilege to be a parent of two Elstree boys and to get to know the school as a Governor too. In both those capacities I have seen first-hand how the School encourages its pupils to make the most of their many and varied opportunities, helps them to grow into confident (but never arrogant) young people.
They understand the value of hard work in attaining high standards, are empathetic and kind, and very much their own people. It has been no surprise therefore to welcome wonderful Elstree girls to Downe who show those very same traits and manage to combine commitment and ambition with courtesy and humility.
Elstree girls bring much and are great assets.
Elstree boys that come to Radley are invariably polite, well-mannered and hard-working. They are prepared to muck in and try everything, and are enthusiastic about the various challenges posed by senior school. They quickly adapt to full boarding, and seem to throw themselves into most things.
Many are humble and self-deprecating about their abilities, whilst being quietly ambitious in all areas. They are not ostentatious, but all seem to have high personal standards, and a willingness to succeed. Whether they are stars academically, on the sports field or in other areas of College life, they are good, solid citizens.
The similarities between Radley and Elstree are many, and the boys that leave Radley are well-rounded and conscientious young men with a strong sense of their place in the world, and the responsibilities that come with that.
I’ve looked after a number of Elstree pupils during my time at Bradfield College – firstly as the housemaster of the Year 9 House Faulkner’s and latterly as the Housemaster of a Senior House.
I have always been struck by the decency of those pupils who have had the privilege of an Elstree education. They are well rounded, polite, well behaved young people with a great attitude to all that they do.
I also believe that those who come to Bradfield are very comfortable in their own skin. They are their own people. That quiet and understated confidence is to be greatly admired and is something that Elstree is quite excellent at instilling in their pupils. I have five boys in my house at the current time who are ex-Elstree. Their interests are quite different – film, cricket, bagpipes, rugby, tennis, drumming – but they pursue those activities, along with their academic work, with great enthusiasm, dignity and humility.
It is always a delight to see Elstree pupils on an interview list. There is a degree of excellence, an incredibly high standard, and a young person who you know will not only play a major role as part of the boarding community, but who will also be a positive influence on all around them.
In a full boarding community, where pupils are living so closely together, there are certain key characteristics that you look for. As a housemaster, what helps a House thrive and feel like a happy, close community where there is a strong sense of camaraderie amongst all the year groups, is having pupils who are confident, kind, empathic, care for each other, and who look forward to throwing themselves into things and getting stuck in. In addition you want pupils who work hard, are determined, independent, and show initiative and strong leadership. You know that you are going to get these qualities in abundance from Elstree pupils.
We are privileged to have welcomed so many girls over the past year from Elstree to our Assessment Days, Musical Theatre Days, Lacrosse camps and many other events at Downe House.
The girls we have met have been confident, well-rounded, kind, and a huge credit to Elstree. They have been unfailingly polite, authentic and we have been impressed by their positive approach to life.
All the girls who have been through our assessment procedure have been offered places, testament to the unparalleled preparation they have received at Elstree.
I have always been deeply impressed by the quality of the pupils coming to us from Elstree. There is no one Elstree ‘type’, just as there is no identikit Shirbornian. They do, however, share certain key characteristics. All have been well taught and come equipped with very sound academic knowledge and understanding. More than that, they know how to learn and realise the importance of hard work and perseverance when the going is tough.
The fact that they conspicuously throw themselves into so many areas of Sherborne life outside the classroom is further testament to the emphasis placed at Elstree upon making the most of the opportunities they are lucky enough to enjoy. Above all, they come with a strong appreciation of the importance of kindness, decency and concern for others and for the world around them.
In my time at Marlborough in the boarding house, classroom and in all the co-curriculum, I have found that boys and girls from Elstree arrive with us well equipped to flourish.
They are not phased by the busy days they face at Marlborough, and they are able to organise themselves effectively to make the most of all that is on offer.
The transition is an easy one as they are grounded with values of kindness and empathy which are precious commodities in a full-boarding school.

Our History
Elstree School was founded in 1848. With the outbreak of war in 1939, staff and 70 boys moved to Woolhampton House in Berkshire.
This fine Georgian house, standing in a 150 acre estate of green parkland and lawns, proved so ideal that Woolhampton House became Elstree’s permanent home at the end of the war, where the School remains today.
The Sanderson Era
Commander Ian Sanderson
The Sanderson Era
Owned and run by the Sanderson family for 100 years, Elstree School was incorporated as a Company Limited by Guarantee in 1961 and is now a registered Charity. Commander Ian Sanderson, the third generation of Sandersons who ran Elstree, remained Headmaster until 1969 when Mr Terrence McMullen became Headmaster. In 1995, Syd Hill took over from Terrence McMullen and he remained Headmaster at Elstree until 2008.
Modernising our facilities
Major developments to School facilities and accommodation have included the renovation of dormitories and bathrooms, a superb new Library, Dining Room, new Junior classroom block, Sports Hall and Science Centre.
In 2015, we opened ‘Bates’ an all-weather pitch which provides three hockey or football pitches and 12 tennis courts.
Modernising our approach
Modernising our approach
In 2019, Elstree’s nursery and pre-preparatory department, previously known as Home Farm officially became Elstree Pre-Prep. New modern classrooms and playgrounds have now been built.
In 2020, Elstree became fully co-educational. Today, girls and boys happily work and play alongside each other.
175 years of Elstree
175 years of Elstree
In 2023 we celebrated the 175th year of Elstree with a special 175 Ball. Over 450 current parents, staff past and present and an army of Old Boys and Girls came together to celebrate the school and honour the role that it has played in the lives of so many.
Thank you
Elstree continues to modernise to offer the very best facilities for a first-class education and a happy, homely environment for children to learn and play. The building works and developments have all been made possible through the generosity of parents, Old Boys, friends of the school and the Bernard Sunley Charitable Foundation.

Bursary Awards
The Governors of Elstree School are committed to broadening access to the school by offering to eligible parents or guardians means-tested financial support with the payment of school fees.
Such support is known as a Bursary and these are awarded in the form of a percentage discount on basic fees payable, depending on the financial, compassionate or other pertinent circumstances of applicants.
Bursary awards are subject to repeat testing of parental means each year and may be varied upwards or downwards, depending on parental circumstances.

Academic Ethos
We aim to inspire a love of learning and for each child to succeed to the very best of their potential.
Our tailored approach means we can personalise each pupil’s academic journey, providing extra support for those who need it and challenging our able and talented pupils; ensuring that they all take pride in their well-earned achievement.
Our Curriculum
We have a broad and varied curriculum. Expert teachers and small class sizes ensure that each child gets the very best care and attention. From the Early Years, we believe children should learn without realising they are doing so. We nurture their curiosity and foster their ambition to set them on a path to success as they grow.
Exceptional staff
Exceptional staff
Our teachers take exceptional care in building their understanding of each pupil. We benefit from a collaborative Common Room, with teaching staff meeting daily to share information that ensures an aligned approach to teaching and supporting the children. Close academic tracking and monitoring, alongside regular communication with home, enables everyone involved to understand how best a child will thrive.
Effort above all is always applauded.
Paving the path to success
Paving the path to success
Outstanding Common Entrance and Scholarship Results in Year 8, are testament to the dedication and expertise of our teaching staff and the School’s exceptional facilities. Elstree pupils go on to the top Senior Schools including Bradfield, Eton, Downe House, Marlborough, Radley, Wellington and Winchester.

Our Community
Elstree welcomes the entire family, not just children into a new class.
With the help of our wonderful parent groups, Friends of Elstree and Elstree Pre-Prep Friends, we create numerous opportunities to get together and contribute to our local community and charities.
With Family Fun Days, Summer Fêtes, Bonfire Night, Dog Shows, Dads’ Curry Nights or the Pre-Prep Quiz – there are social gatherings galore, not to mention weekly sports matches and regular coffee mornings, school performances and concerts.
Keeping in touch
Keeping in touch
We are proud to maintain a lasting bond with so many Elstree Old Boys and Girls. With regular reunions, we enjoy hearing how they progress at Senior School and in their chosen careers.
Over 10% of our current pupils are the sons and daughters of Old Boys and Girls, and we are delighted that the happy childhood memories of so many parents are ones they will meaningfully share with their own children.
Giving back
Giving back
Our pupils join us in giving back to the wider community and supporting local charities, from making Food Bank donations, to gifting shoeboxes of thoughtful presents to children facing hardship at Christmas. Pupils also undertake their own individual charitable endeavours throughout the year.
Every term we also come together (with a great many dogs!) for pupil, parent and staff Wellbeing Walk around the school grounds – a glorious moment of outdoor goodness.

Leavers’ Entertainment
Last night our Year 8s treated us to their final performance in the McMullen Hall.
In true cabaret style, parents were invited to enjoy a night of funny sketches and nostalgia. With an emotional mix of humour, tomfoolery and sincerity, the boys and girls acted out scenes and songs including Cinnamon Yoghurt, Brain Surgery, Hey Marcello, Risk and Wear Sunscreen.
This was a relaxed and funny evening full of sentiment and pride. Very well done to all who took part and a huge thanks to Mr Pugsley and Mr Spencer for their brilliant effort through rehearsals and on the night itself – great fun for all!

Leavers’ Service
Having been awarded their ESA ties by Mr Bates in the Rose Garden, our Year 8s set off for their last service at Douai Abbey. Joined by parents, staff and Prep School pupils, we enjoyed a memorable service with wonderful hymns, readings and prayers. James McKinnel @winchestercollege gave a sermon of joy and thanks, reminding us of the wonderful childhood memories our Year 8s will look back on and expressing their hope and anticipation as they come to the end of their time at Elstree and look forward to new adventures.
Bidding a fond farewell to our Year 8s and their families, the Rose Garden was filled with memories, friendship, laughter and a sense of one happy chapter ending, and a lot to look forward to. Well done to all these wonderful boys and girls – come back and see us soon!

Opening of the new Pre-Prep Outdoor Classroom
Once again, it was wonderful to welcome back Elstree Old Boys Freddie and Louis, (Elstree 2015 Leavers), who were busy building a fabulous new outdoor classroom in the Early Years’ Woods during the Summer holidays.
This is their third Smiley Bespoke project at Elstree this year, having already completed the renovation of the Harry Shapland Adventure Playground and the Castle in the Pre-Prep playground. Freddie and Louis are so talented and hard working and we are incredibly grateful to them both.
The children were thrilled to hold an opening ceremony during the first week of term, including the cutting of a ribbon and are clearly loving their new outdoor space to learn and thrive.

Creative Arts
Music, art and drama help children to develop skills, attitudes and attributes that can support learning in other subject areas.
These include their ability to listen, concentrate and express themselves, also developing their creativity and sensitivity towards others.
Music
Music
Each year group has two lessons with a music specialist every week. They develop their understanding and appreciation of a wide range of different types of music and are given the chance to participate and perform in groups, and as soloists.
From Year 1, children have the opportunity to start instrumental lessons with the peripatetic teachers at Elstree. In Year 2, all children learn the recorder. Concerts take place in the Summer Term with all children participating and showcasing songs they have learnt throughout the year. In Years 1 and 2, children can also join the Pre-Prep Choir which meets weekly.
Art
Art
Art features every day, whether it is drawing, painting, collaging, pottery or making things – from sculptures using items found in the woods to crafting a set of houses to re-enact The Great Fire of London.
Class teachers teach art lessons. These follow the termly theme and incorporate a range of artistic skills. Children are encouraged to be creative and to express themselves, with many opting to complete additional art activities in their ‘choosing’ time. All of the children take great pride in seeing their art displayed in and around the Pre-Prep.
Drama
Drama
Children from Nursery to Year 2 have a weekly drama lesson which takes place in the main school. This helps to develop the children’s confidence in speaking, listening and performing. Where possible, links are made in Drama lessons to the children’s topic that they are learning.
The Christmas Nativity Play is one of the highlights of the year, providing the opportunity for all of the children to perform on the stage. In addition to the play, children from each year take part in our annual Poetry Performance and Reception to Year 2 children perform in Prep School assemblies, allowing the children to become familiar with larger audiences.
